newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel breaks 3.32 to the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel breaks 3.32 to the dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate fell to a new all time-low against the dollar on Monday following the rise of the U.S. currency in world markets, dealers said.
"The main reason for the shekel's decline was the dollar's rise abroad," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"The basket is still trading at seven percent below the diagonal rate. The Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market again on a relatively small scale," he said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
Dealers estimated that the Bank of Israel bought less than $100 million in foreign currency on Monday.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3210 shekels against 3.3140 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6287 shekels against 3.6272 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7206 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7242 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0159 shekels against 2.0265 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3180 shekels.
